chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"You should not accuse the one you have trusted, nor should you trust the treacherous one whom you have tested."
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ethical principle regarding trusting and accusing others based on experience?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on leases and trusts, this hadith establishes a nuanced legal and ethical principle regarding the presumption of innocence (*al-asl bi al-sihha*) in commercial and social dealings. It warns against the injustice of accusing a trusted agent (*amin*) without cause, while simultaneously cautioning against the negligence of re-entrusting a known betrayer (*khiyan*), thereby balancing probity with practical experience (*tajriba*).
